headline: FBI probes dark web service selling 153M+ drivers licenses from US & Canada
summary: The service, Nexus, offers digital scans of IDs, including high-ranking US officials, with data allegedly sourced from a major identity verification company.
details: A new dark web service, "Nexus," is selling digital scans of over 153 million drivers licenses from people in the United States and Canada. The service also offers millions of other ID cards, travel documents, and medical cards, totaling over 170 million individuals.

The FBI's New Orleans field office has launched an official inquiry into the source of these images. The data reportedly includes licenses for high-ranking US government officials, such as Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

Nexus claims the images are from an active breach at a "major identity verification company" based in Louisiana, whose clients include Fortune 500 companies. Data is continuously exfiltrated, with nearly 400,000 new records added in 24 hours.

KrebsOnSecurity confirmed the presence of their own license and those of friends/family, noting timestamps on the images correspond to travel dates. The records include front and back scans, as well as infrared and ultraviolet versions.

headline_marked: [[Apple Maps renames Lake Ontario]] to 'Lake America' after Trump order
headline: Apple Maps renames Lake Ontario to 'Lake America' after Trump order
summary: Apple follows Google in adopting the new name for the Great Lake, a change stemming from an executive order during a trade dispute with Canada. Canadian and international versions of the app show different names.
details: Apple Maps has officially changed the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America, following Google's earlier update. This change comes after an executive order signed by President Donald Trump amidst a trade dispute with Canada.
While US versions of Apple Maps display 'Lake America,' the Canadian version still shows 'Lake Ontario.' International versions of the app reportedly show both names.

This isn't the first such change; both Apple and Google previously renamed the Gulf of Mexico to the 'Gulf of America' after a similar executive order. Interestingly, MapQuest has refused to adopt these name changes.
